name: strategy.output
description: Advisory quality screen for a business-strategy artifact (strategy argument, 'only' statement, strategy document, or strategy review) produced under business-strategy-os. Asks whether it is a real strategy or an average one. Section counting and banned-phrase linting stay in code (strategy_lint.py); only judgment is asked here.

category_customer_frame.instructions: The artifact names the category the way a customer shopping for it would name it (what they compare against), not by delivery format, technology or industry jargon.

genuine_disagreement.instructions: The artifact states a specific belief about how the category should work that most current competitors would reject in good faith. It is not a platitude every competitor already claims (quality, service, innovation, customer focus).

only_claim_holds.instructions: The artifact's 'we are the only X who Y, so customers get Z' claim (or its equivalent) would be conceded as true by the fiercest competitor: Y is something competitors do not do, and Z is value customers cannot get elsewhere.

tradeoffs_named.instructions: The artifact names concrete things the business will stop doing, refuse to do, or change, not only things it will add.

concrete_innovation.instructions: The differentiating action is a concrete, observable innovation (product feature, production method, route to market, bundling, branding taken to an extreme, targeting, customer experience, pricing or culture), not a claimed virtue.

externally_visible.instructions: The execution names delivery and communication actions specific enough that a customer, investor or partner could see the strategy just by looking at the business.

strategy_not_goal.instructions: The artifact explains how the business will win. It is not a goal, target, vision statement or wish list presented as a strategy.

specificity.instructions: How specific is this strategy to this business in this category
criteria: Boilerplate that would fit almost any company
Fits most companies in the category
Some specifics, but the core claim fits competitors
Specific to this business, with one generic core element
Specific: a direct competitor could not claim it
Specific, evidenced, and a competitor would reject it in good faith

rules.reason: category is framed by format or jargon, not by what the customer shops for
no belief a competitor would reject: this is the category average
the 'only' claim would not survive the fiercest-competitor test
no trade-offs: nothing is stopped, refused or changed
differentiation is a claimed virtue, not an observable innovation
execution is not visible to an outsider
this is a goal or wish list, not a way to win
strategy is not specific enough to this business
specificity answer distribution is not concentrated

notes.bar: Pass line is above 0.9 for every noul and a specificity mean above 4.50 (the work-criteria.json bar).

notes.planted_failure: A boilerplate strategy (customer-focused, high quality, innovative, grow 20%) must ESCALATE on genuine_disagreement, only_claim_holds and specificity; the red/green pair lives in capabilities/skills/business-strategy-os/references/jev-fixtures/.
